public_rationale: Models adjusted their performance to avoid a stated consequence, with the consequence reversed in the comparison condition. That contradicts the ordinary behavioral reading of not calculating consequences at all. A narrower claim about an unspecified internal mechanism remains unsettled.
limitations: The consequences were supplied explicitly in a simplified task.
The result does not demonstrate human-like understanding or generally reliable foresight.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: LLMs do not calculate the consequences of their actions at all.

statement.excerpt: Worse, they do not actually calculate the consequences of their actions at all.

our_interpretation: The ordinary testable reading is that LLMs cannot work out how an action changes an outcome and use that consequence to guide their choice.
The categorical phrase at all makes a controlled demonstration of consequence-sensitive choice sufficient to contradict this reading. It does not require reliable planning in every situation.
This does not equate successful behavior with consciousness or a human-like internal model.
The target is the December 2024 capability snapshot available before the December 12 post, using the current research reporting window.
criteria.support_condition: Controlled tests across the relevant models find no ability to use action-outcome relationships, beyond superficial response patterns, to guide choices.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Controlled experiments show models selecting actions according to their predicted consequences, including changing behavior when the consequence of the same action changes.
